# Results — Study 850 (Airline Operational Meltdown)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: **a
very public operational meltdown — a multi-day grounding, a mass-cancellation collapse,
a viral PR disaster — is a reputational shock that dents the implicated airline's own
stock**, both around the event and as a slow bleed over the following month. Single-name
market-model event study (MacKinlay 1997) on the implicated carrier (LUV/DAL/UAL/AAL/BA),
benchmarked to SPY. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped) — all numbers below are as-of 2026-06-30.*

*Fingerprint `6ce22fa749d2` (SPY) · `710a0aa31fcf` (LUV) · `24f189e4696e` (DAL) ·
`d6b73e44a59c` (UAL) · `0b16d927b778` (AAL) · `4be94ccd2936` (BA).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`), **3,141 rows each, 2014-01-02 → 2026-06-30**: SPY (benchmark) + LUV / DAL / UAL / AAL / BA |
| Meltdown table | **hardcoded** table of **10 famous airline / Boeing operational meltdowns 2016-08-08 → 2024-07-19**, each tagged with the single **implicated ticker** and a one-line public-record source note (8-K/DOT/FAA/NTSB + contemporary wire coverage) in [`airline_meltdown/data.py`](../airline_meltdown/data.py) |
| Events scored | **9 of 10** — the **Spirit-2021 (SAVE)** meltdown is dropped: Spirit filed Chapter 11 in Nov-2024, its stock was cancelled on the 2025 reorganisation, and `SAVE` is fully delisted from Yahoo Finance (no history returned). Named honestly, never zero-filled |
| Model | Market-model event study: OLS `alpha, beta` on SPY over a **120-session estimation window** ending **10 sessions before** each event (uncontaminated by the shock); abnormal return `= r_stock − (alpha + beta·r_SPY)`; CAR summed over four horizons |
| Statistics | One-sample *t* across the (independent, non-overlapping) events for each horizon's CAR; Wilson interval on the down-hit rate; a **same-ticker random-date permutation placebo** (5,000 draws — each event keeps its ticker/beta/vol, gets a random pseudo-date); Newey-West *t* reported as a cross-check (unstable at n=9, not the primary) |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the meltdown's public date is **snapped to the first NYSE session on/after it** (a Friday-evening/weekend collapse rolls to the next open) — zero look-ahead, since the collapse is public before that session's close. The timer shorts the implicated stock at that session's close, covers `hold` sessions later; 2 × one-way cost × NAV + borrow on the short leg |
| Survivorship (named) | the implicated tickers are the *current listed* entities; a carrier that delisted (Spirit/SAVE) simply drops out — the basket answers "do **today's listed** carriers' stocks react to their own meltdown", tilting the sample toward survivors that weathered the shock |

## The headline — cross-event mean market-model CAR, by horizon

Per-event CAR (bps), market-model abnormal return vs SPY:

| date | ticker | day 0 | week [0..+4] | month [0..+21] | drift [+1..+21] |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2016-08-08 | DAL (IT/power outage) | −23.9 | −184.9 | **+938.1** | +962.0 |
| 2017-01-30 | DAL (IT outage) | −331.1 | −491.3 | −769.9 | −438.8 |
| 2017-04-10 | UAL (Dao dragging) | +69.8 | −17.9 | **+506.4** | +436.7 |
| 2019-03-11 | **BA (MAX grounding)** | −751.0 | −1554.9 | **−2450.4** | −1699.4 |
| 2021-10-11 | LUV (Oct meltdown) | −280.8 | −813.4 | −928.4 | −647.6 |
| 2021-11-01 | AAL (Halloween meltdown) | +287.4 | +1119.9 | −1038.8 | −1326.2 |
| 2022-12-27 | LUV (Christmas collapse) | −564.8 | −944.7 | −422.5 | +142.3 |
| 2024-01-08 | **BA (door-plug blowout)** | −952.9 | −1548.9 | **−2391.0** | −1438.1 |
| 2024-07-19 | DAL (CrowdStrike) | +193.9 | −12.5 | −1038.6 | −1232.5 |

| horizon | n | mean CAR | one-sample *t* | (NW *t*) | down-hit | placebo *p* (left) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **day 0** | 9 | **−261.5 bps** | **−1.82** | −4.28 | 6/9 (Wilson [35%, 88%]) | **0.002** |
| week [0..+4] | 9 | −494.3 bps | −1.76 | −4.59 | 8/9 (Wilson [56%, 98%]) | — |
| **month [0..+21]** | 9 | **−843.9 bps** | **−2.24** | −2.74 | 7/9 (Wilson [45%, 94%]) | **0.014** |
| drift [+1..+21] | 9 | −582.4 bps | −1.88 | −2.18 | 6/9 (Wilson [35%, 88%]) | 0.056 |

At face value this looks like a hit: the average meltdown stock is down **−261 bps** on
day 0 and **−844 bps** over the following month, the sign matches the claim, the month
CAR crosses the desk's |*t*| ≥ 2 bar (*t* = −2.24), and the random-date placebo is
emphatic (day-0 *p* = 0.002, month *p* = 0.014 — a random calendar of the same 9
tickers almost never produces a drop this size). **But that aggregate is not what the
folklore claims it is** — see the robustness split below.

## Robustness — the aggregate is a Boeing-grounding effect, not a reputational one

Two of the nine events are **Boeing 737-MAX groundings** (2019 fatal-crash grounding,
2024 door-plug blowout). A MAX grounding is not a "sentiment/reputation" shock — it is a
**fundamental cash-flow event**: the entire product line is grounded for months and
deliveries halt, a genuine hit to earnings. Those two events dominate everything:

| subsample | day-0 CAR (*t*) | month CAR (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|
| all 9 events | −261.5 bps (−1.82) | **−843.9 bps (−2.24)** |
| **airlines only (no BA, n=7)** | −92.8 bps (**−0.79**) | −393.4 bps (**−1.30**) |
| Boeing only (n=2) | −851.9 bps (−8.44*) | −2420.7 bps (−81.5*) |

*(*Boeing-only *t* on n=2 is not a meaningful inference — shown only to display the
magnitude.)*

Strip the two Boeing groundings and the **pure airline operational-meltdown** thesis —
IT outages, mass-cancellation collapses, the United dragging PR crisis — is **not
significant at any horizon** (day-0 *t* = −0.79, month *t* = −1.30). Individual airline
meltdowns are genuinely mixed: Delta's 2016 outage and United's 2017 dragging crisis
both had **positive** one-month CARs (+938, +506 bps) as the stock shrugged the episode
off inside a rallying tape. **Leave-one-out** confirms the full-sample significance is
load-bearing on the Boeing pair: dropping BA-2019 gives *t* = −1.78, dropping BA-2024
gives *t* = −1.77 — either one alone drops the month CAR below the |*t*| ≥ 2 bar; the
airline events, by contrast, mostly leave it near or above 2 when dropped. The
significance **does not hold across sub-eras** either (pre-2022 month *t* = −1.26). This
is the hallmark of a **Weak** stamp: a directionally-correct, economically-sensible tug
whose apparent strength is a *composition artifact* of two fundamental events
masquerading as the reputational claim.

## The timer — short the meltdown stock

Short the implicated stock at the snap-session close (the meltdown is public — zero
look-ahead), hold `hold` sessions, cover. Net = 2 × one-way 5 bps + 300 bps/yr borrow on
the short leg.

| hold | gross short | net short | *t* (net) | win rate | airlines-only net (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 d | +213.4 bps | +197.5 bps | +0.87 | 78% | −18.2 bps (−0.08) |
| 10 d | +258.9 bps | +237.0 bps | +1.09 | 67% | +96.3 bps (+0.37) |
| 21 d | +176.1 bps | +141.1 bps | +0.44 | 56% | −25.7 bps (−0.07) |

The short is **positive in-sample at every horizon** and survives costs+borrow — but it
is never close to significant (best *t* = +1.09 on n=9), and it is again **entirely
Boeing-concentrated**: drop the two groundings and the airlines-only short collapses to
roughly zero (−18 / +96 / −26 bps, |*t*| ≤ 0.4). It is a nine-observation number resting
on two events, which is the textbook definition of a **Fragile** edge — before even
noting that shorting an airline into a well-publicised meltdown means paying up for
hard-to-borrow at exactly the moment every other trader wants the same short.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic market + multi-stock factor panel with scheduled pseudo-meltdown events
and a TUNABLE planted day-0 drop (plus a small persistent bleed); no network.

| world | day-0 one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.08** (sd 1.05), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **1/20** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.03 (seed 850) | **−8.48** (mean −283.5 bps) |

The detector sits at zero on the null (1/20 crossings ≈ the expected 5% false-positive
rate at n=9) and lights up sharply on a planted drop. *(A faithful-engine / power check
only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The full 9-event aggregate is directionally right and nominally
  significant at the one-month horizon (mean CAR **−843.9 bps**, one-sample *t* =
  **−2.24**, random-date placebo *p* = **0.014**; day-0 placebo *p* = **0.002**) — but it
  is **not robust**. It is driven almost entirely by the **two Boeing 737-MAX groundings**
  (a fundamental product-line/earnings shock, *not* the reputational-sentiment mechanism
  the folklore claims): the airlines-only subsample is insignificant at every horizon
  (day-0 *t* = −0.79, month *t* = −1.30), several individual airline meltdowns had
  *positive* one-month CARs, leave-one-out on either Boeing event drops the month *t*
  below 2, and the effect does not hold in the pre-2022 sub-era. So there is a real,
  modest "big shocks dent the stock" tendency — but the specific "operational meltdown =
  reputational stock hit" claim does **not** clear the bar once the fundamental groundings
  are separated out.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Shorting the meltdown stock is positive net-of-costs at
  every horizon in-sample (best *t* = +1.09, n=9) yet never significant and, again,
  entirely Boeing-concentrated — airlines-only it is ≈0. A nine-event edge resting on two
  fundamental groundings, needing a hard-to-borrow short into a crowded trade, is not
  something to bank.
- **"Does an operational meltdown dent the airline's stock?" — MIXED.** A grounding of
  the product line (Boeing MAX) genuinely does, because it is fundamental; a cancellation
  collapse or IT outage or PR firestorm at a still-flying carrier mostly **fades** — the
  reputational-shock version of the story is not detectable in this tradable sample at
  n=9. Low N is the honest limitation, not a hidden strength.
